review_comments: [team convention] Round money only with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent). Python's round() and a bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and give wrong invoice totals.

item.title: Round monetary results with the project's money helper
item.description: The first attempt returned an unrounded Decimal division and was rejected because the team requires ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent).
item.content: When a function returns a money value, wrap the final computation in the repository's round_money helper rather than returning a raw Decimal or using Python's round()/quantize(), which use banker's rounding. Check ledgerly/money.py for the canonical helpers (ZERO, to_money, round_money) and reuse them.

item.title: Read the money module before implementing financial logic
item.description: The agent only discovered round_money after the review comment, though it was already imported in invoice.py.
item.content: Before writing any arithmetic on prices or totals, inspect the existing money utilities and sibling functions (e.g. line_total, invoice_total) to mirror their rounding and conversion conventions. Existing imports in the target file are a strong hint about required helpers.

item.title: Handle empty collections with the project's zero constant
item.description: Returning ZERO for invoices without lines matched the spec and the codebase's convention.
item.content: Guard against division by zero by checking the total quantity first and returning the module's ZERO constant, keeping the return type consistent (Decimal) across all branches.
